title: Dosage and styles
subtitle: Sweetness and colour
objectives: Explain blanc de blancs, blanc de noirs and rosé

steps.title: Dosage
steps.body: After disgorgement, the liqueur d'expédition, wine with sugar, tops up the bottle. It balances acidity and adds to the flavour development over time through Maillard reactions between sugar and amino acids. The trend is towards lower dosage, but very low dosage can taste austere in a young, high-acid wine.

steps.title: Styles
steps.body: Brut Nature has 0 to 3 g/l; Extra Brut up to 6; Brut up to 12; Extra Dry 12 to 17; Dry or Sec 17 to 32; Demi-Sec 32 to 50; Doux over 50. Blanc de Blancs is made only from white grapes, usually Chardonnay. Blanc de Noirs is white wine from black grapes. Rosé can be blended, with still red wine, or saignée.
steps.highlight: Blanc de Blancs, Blanc de Noirs, Rosé

steps.prompt: Which are true about Blanc de Noirs?
options: It's a white wine made from black grapes
It can use Pinot Noir and Meunier
Its colour comes from gentle pressing
steps.explanation: Blanc de Noirs can be any sweetness level. Its pale colour comes from gentle pressing of black grapes.

steps.body: A Demi-Sec Champagne is underrated with fruit tarts and spicy food. Extra Brut and Brut Nature shine with oysters and raw fish.

steps.prompt: Which dosage term is drier: Extra Brut or Extra Dry?
steps.explanation: Extra Brut has up to 6 g/l; Extra Dry has 12 to 17 g/l.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dosage balances acidity and helps flavour develop
Sweetness terms run from Brut Nature to Doux
Blanc de Blancs, Blanc de Noirs and Rosé describe grapes and colour
